results.title: POSCO workers vote to accept pay deal
results.content: Unionized workers at Korean steelmaker POSCO have voted to accept the company's pay offer after five months of negotiations, the union said Saturday. Union members approved a 2.6 percent increase in base pay, a one-off payment of 6.2 million won ($4,600) and improved benefits in a vote held Saturday. The union had initially demanded a 7.1 percent increase in base pay, a performance bonus equivalent to 600 percent of base pay, 50 company shares per worker and a holiday bonus equivalent to 200 percent of base pay. It also raised concerns over staffing shortages and aging facilities, saying they could increase the risk of workplace accidents. Management's previous offer included a 2.5 percent increase in base pay and a one-off payment of 5 million won. results.title: Foreign tourists navigate complicated maze upon arriving at Seoul Station
results.content: A Brazilian couple visiting Korea for the first time found themselves in a state of panic almost as soon as they arrived at Seoul Station after taking the Airport Railroad Express (AREX) from Incheon International Airport. Maria Diatrix, 61, and her husband stood in front of a transfer passageway with three large suitcases, unable to get through the ticket gates because the QR code on their express train tickets was not being recognized. As crowds streamed through three separate passageways leading to Seoul Metro Lines 1 and 4 and the Airport Railroad, the couple stood helplessly in front of the gates. They pressed the assistance button, only to receive an announcement over the speaker advising them to exit via the second basement level or purchase new single-journey transit cards. results.title: Yangyang airport set to resume international flights
results.content: Gangwon Province is stepping up efforts to attract Chinese tourists and develop travel packages ahead of the resumption of international flights at Yangyang International Airport. With regular international services set to resume after more than three years, attention is turning to whether the airport can attract more foreign visitors and finally overcome its reputation as an "international airport in name only." According to Gangwon Province and the Gangwon Tourism Organization on Thursday, the province invited four Chinese social media influencers for a five-day familiarization tour beginning Nov. 22, in cooperation with the Korea Tourism Organization and Korea Airports Corporation. The influencers visited major tourist destinations in Gangneung, Sokcho, Goseong, Yangyang and Pyeongchang to introduce the region to Chinese travelers. results.title: Lee vows all-out efforts to lead AI race at data center groundbreaking in Gangwon
results.content: President Lee Jae Myung pledged Saturday to mobilize all government resources to make Korea a leading country in the global artificial intelligence (AI) race, as he attended a groundbreaking ceremony for GS Group's AI data center in the eastern province of Gangwon, his office said. GS Group is building the 2.4-gigawatt AI data center campus in the eastern city of Donghae as part of the government's three major megaprojects announced in June. Once completed, the facility is expected to become one of Asia's largest AI infrastructure complexes. "The project will be the first megaproject in the Gangwon region and become Asia's largest AI infrastructure facility," Cheong Wa Dae said. "It will serve as a key driver of new growth and vitality for the regional economy." results.title: Foreign workers demand right to switch workplaces without letter of release
results.content: Many foreign workers in Korea are stuck in their current jobs without the freedom to seek better employment, due to a regulation that a union of foreign language teachers wants abolished. For many foreign workers living in Korea on an E-series visa, their continued stay in the country is tied directly to their jobs. In the eventuality that they have to change jobs in the middle of a contract, they must seek consent from their employer through a document known as a letter of release. Korean employers effectively sponsor visas for foreign employees by guaranteeing their status in the country. This leaves foreign employees vulnerable to exploitation by employers, who wield disproportionate control over their working conditions, wages and even housing. results.title: 'Sea of Whales' asks whether Jeju waters can be home for dolphins
results.content: A filmmaker who spent a decade documenting dolphins off Jeju Island asks whether the sea can be a home where humans and whales live together. “Sea of Whales” began as a search for the gray whale, which has not been seen in Korean waters since 1977. Despite having the word "whales" in its title, director Lee Jeong-joon’s Sea of Whales actually chronicles the lives of roughly 120 Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins living off the coast of Jeju Island. The species has been protected by the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries since 2012. The director said the project grew out of curiosity. “As a documentary director, I realized how little information there was about the whales living in our own waters,” he said after a press screening in Seoul on Thursday. “I moved to Jeju in 2015 to document how they live. results.title: More than a decade after pilot dream, Global Korea Awards winner defends Korea's skies in F-16s
results.content: Lee Seung-jin won the Model High School Student award at the second Korea Multicultural Youth Award — now known as the Global Korea Award — in 2013. Three years later, he told The Korea Times his dream was to become an Air Force pilot. A decade on, the 29-year-old is living that dream. As a captain with the 19th Fighter Wing, Lee leads a flight of four F-16 fighter jets and helps defend Korea’s airspace every day. “I take pride in every mission because this is a job that not just anyone can do or is trusted with, and because I longed to be in this position,” Lee said in an interview with The Korea Times. results.title: Internet Post Office hacking leaks personal data of at least 113,000 customers
results.content: A hacking attack on the Internet Post Office has exposed the personal information of at least 113,855 customers, with the full scope of the breach still under investigation, the postal service said Saturday. The Korea Post, under the Ministry of Science and ICT, said it has confirmed that hackers had accessed mailing records containing customers' personal information and is working to determine the full scope of the breach. The attackers accessed the mobile Internet Post Office's delivery location change service and viewed the names, addresses and phone numbers of recipients of registered mail being delivered between Nov. 17 and 24. An analysis of data from a single day alone found that 113,855 people had their information exposed. results.title: Stock loans fall to 13-month low amid wild volatility
results.content: Stock loans in Korea fell to a 13-month low this week amid increased volatility in stock markets, industry data showed Saturday. The amount of outstanding margin loans came to 25.04 trillion won ($18.7 billion) on Friday, marking the lowest level since Oct. 28 last year, according to the data compiled by the Korea Financial Investment Association. The tally came as volatility heightened in local stock markets this week. After hitting a record peak in June, the benchmark KOSPI has slumped, mainly due to investment fears over artificial intelligence. This week alone, trading curbs on the stock markets were activated four times due to wild swings.

results.title: N. Korea, Russia hold economic cooperation meeting, agree to boost joint projects
results.content: North Korea and Russia have held a committee meeting on economic cooperation in Pyongyang and agreed to step up joint projects in various economic fields, the North's state media reported Saturday. The 13th meeting of the bilateral intergovernmental committee for cooperation in trade, economy, science and technology was held at the Pyongyang Assembly Hall on Friday, according to the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA). Yun Jong-Ho, North Korea's minister of external economic relations and chairman of the committee on the North Korean side, and Russian Natural Resources and Ecology Minister Alexandr Kozlov, who heads the Russian side, attended the meeting, along with Russian Ambassador to the DPRK Andrey Podelyshev and other officials, it added. results.title: Spy agency says monitoring developments amid speculation over NK leader's possible China visit
results.content: South Korea's spy agency said Saturday it is closely monitoring developments amid speculation that North Korean leader Kim Jong-un could make another visit to China. "We are monitoring various developments," the National Intelligence Service (NIS) said in response to a Yonhap News Agency inquiry about media reports that Kim's visit to China could be imminent. Speculation over a possible visit has centered on Chinese President Xi Jinping's briefing to President Lee Jae Myung on recent developments in North Korea-China relations during their summit in Shenzhen last week on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. Some observers believe Xi's remarks could be interpreted as pointing to the possibility of a visit to China by Kim or another senior North Korean official. results.title: The 4 deaths of Gong Yoo
results.content: This week, I’ve sat in four different classrooms in Seoul, with young adults from all over the world, watching "Train to Busan" as part of our exploration of modern Korean society. A strange choice, you might think, but the messages and critiques are all there bubbling away below the tension created by tight spaces and savage beasts. Students from Kazakhstan cried; Americans whooped, cheered and gesticulated wildly as the movie progressed (Ma Dong-seok’s body generated considerable noise); some Indonesian students ate hamburgers and hid behind their hands; a few Korean students mentioned the continued use of "shinpa" (emotional blackmail) in Korean movies and lamented the gender representation; others told me somewhat proudly they were from Busan. results.title: Indian businessman turns 27 years in Korea into mission of giving back
results.content: After 27 years of building a life and business in Korea, Indian entrepreneur Sanghrajka Himansu Naresh is giving back to the Seoul community he calls home, donating essential supplies to vulnerable residents and personally visiting welfare facilities to ensure his contributions meet their most pressing needs. Naresh, 46, recently donated 10 million won ($6,800) worth of goods to two welfare institutions in Yongsan District, where he has lived since arriving in Korea in 1999. The donation, presented last week with the district office, included medical equipment for people with severe disabilities and winter apparel for children at a local orphanage. At Yeongnak Ania's House, a facility for people with severe disabilities, he donated a specialized medical bed and two oxygen concentrators to improve care for its residents. results.title: [EXPLAINER] Why Korean presidents keep showing up at traditional markets
results.content: President Lee Jae Myung made an unannounced stop at a traditional market in Seoul’s Eunpyeong District on Wednesday after attending a roundtable on public housing in the area, in keeping with a longstanding practice among Korean presidents of visiting markets to gauge how people are getting by. At Daerim Alley Market, which opened in 1979, Lee asked shopkeepers how business was going as he bought cherries and bungeoppang — a fish-shaped filled pancake that is popular as a winter snack in Korea. The president also heard suggestions for upgrading market facilities and making them more convenient for shoppers, according to Cheong Wa Dae. results.title: Hongdae live clubs face inspection blitz as minister who promised to lift dance ban set to leave
results.content: Live music venues near western Seoul's Hongik University are pushing back against a flurry of regulatory inspections that have forced some venues to turn standing concerts into seated shows, reigniting debate over Korea's restrictions on dancing. The increased scrutiny comes amid growing calls to overhaul regulations that prohibit customers from dancing at establishments registered as general restaurants, a category under which many live music clubs operate. The neighborhood in front of the university, often referred to as Hongdae, has been the heart of Korea's independent music scene since the mid-1990s. results.title: Foreign residents in Incheon step beyond high-rises to explore nearby islands
results.content: For many foreign residents living in Incheon’s gleaming, master-planned business districts, daily life revolves around glass office towers, international schools and expressways linking them to Seoul. Last week, a group of foreign residents traded that futuristic skyline for coastal boardwalks and tidal flats, exploring the islands and maritime heritage tucked just minutes from their doorstep. Thirty-nine international residents of the Incheon Free Economic Zone took part in a field excursion organized by the zone’s authority to deepen their connection to the port city’s coastal geography and local history. Departing from G-Tower in Songdo, the participants spent the day touring Muui Island and Yeongjong Island, two coastal destinations on Korea’s west coast. results.title: International Bar Association warns of 'dangerous precedent' in Cho impeachment push
results.content: The International Bar Association (IBA) has expressed concern over the proposed impeachment of Supreme Court Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae, stressing the importance of judicial independence and the separation of powers.
